item.title: Green Cities Can Make Room for New Homes and the Farms That Feed Them
item.description: A field at the edge of a growing city may be worth far more than its market price suggests. It may produce vegetables sold in nearby markets, support local livelihoods and provide green space in an increasingly built-up environment. It can also help cities manage water, adapt to climate shocks and strengthen local food supplies. […]

item.title: New Biodiversity Pledges Emerge at COP17, But Funding Gap Persists
item.description: This first part of a two-part series on biodiversity finance at CBD COP17 examines the status of finance mobilisation and new funding commitments.

item.title: UN rights office warns of deepening displacement ‘nightmare’ in Gaza
item.description: Israeli forces continue to push Palestinians into ever-smaller areas of the Gaza Strip while destroying civilian infrastructure and attacking displacement sites, the UN human rights office, OHCHR, warned on Friday amid concerns of ethnic cleansing.

item.title: Yemen war makes reaching assistance too dangerous for many
item.description: More than 280,000 people have now been displaced by fighting in Yemen and many vulnerable people are unable to access lifesaving relief because it is too dangerous to do so, the UN refugee agency (UNHCR) said on Friday.

item.title: DR Congo: Hunger deepens for millions amid conflict, Ebola and climate shocks
item.description: More than 28 million people in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) are not getting enough to eat and the number is expected to tick up in the coming months, according to the latest alert from the IPC global food security monitor.

item.title: World News in Brief: 300,000 displaced in Lebanon, Türk ‘deeply concerned’ over Novaya Gazeta closure, $50 million refugee appeal, World Cities Day
item.description: More than 300,000 people displaced since early March remain internally displaced in Lebanon, where the humanitarian crisis is “far from over,” according to the UN’s aid coordination office (OCHA).

item.title: Ukraine: Oleshky ceasefire offers ‘hope’ for civilians as attacks on aid vehicles continue
item.description: Each day the ceasefire in Oleshky holds means hope for civilians in the city, the UN’s top humanitarian official said, stressing that those wishing to leave must be able to do so safely and voluntarily.

item.title: Women and Girls’ Death Toll in Armed Conflict Doubles since 2021
item.description: At least 25 women and girls are killed every day as civilian deaths mount, sexual violence rises, and women remain largely excluded from peace negotiations.
